subject: Multi-year commitment: sinking-fund commit schedule & rollover mechanics
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Committed spend mechanics — multi-year plan question

Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Acme team liked the predictable latency numbers. Procurement asked me to surface a few specific questions around how a multi-year committed spend could be structured to support our seasonality. High level: we want a 36-month commitment but with a front-loaded ramp in year 1, then measured growth years 2–3. Key asks:

- Can committed units be structured as a sinking fund / pre-funded bucket that decays monthly rather than a single upfront tranche?
- Is there a rollover cap for unused committed dollars between quarters/years?
- How do you handle true-ups if actual consumption ramps faster than the committed velocity?
- What discount breaks do you apply for year commitments vs multi-year?

Procurement attached a simple forecast (procurement_request.xlsx). Can you propose the mechanics and a sample amortization/discount model?

Thanks — Samantha

--
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Procurement
Acme Analytics
Attachments: procurement_request.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@acme-analytics.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Committed spend mechanics — multi-year plan question

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks. I sketched two pragmatic options that match what others have used when seasonality is important: a) a "sinking-fund" prepay that amortizes monthly against committed velocity and b) a laddered tranche approach with explicit cliffs and replenishment triggers. Below is a concise summary and a sample amortization (attached: RAMP_TABLE.xlsx and SOW_draft.pdf).

1) Sinking-fund (recommended for forecasting simplicity)
- You prepay an upfront wallet equal to an agreed % of total committed value (example: 60% up front).
- Wallet balance is drawn down monthly based on committed velocity (committed tokens/month).
- Unused portion at quarter boundary can roll forward subject to a cap (we typically cap carry-forward at 20% of the next quarter commitment).
- Quarterly true-up: if actual consumption > committed for that quarter, consumption pulls first from wallet (if available), then triggers an overage charge or top-up at a pre-negotiated rate.

2) Laddered cliffs (preferred when finance needs discrete invoices)
- Commit is split into N tranches (e.g., 3 annual tranches or 6 semiannual).
- Each tranche unlocks with a cliff schedule; unused portion can be applied as credit to next tranche up to a carry-forward cap.
- Can include an early-burn accelerator (higher discount applied if usage exceeds X% of committed run-rate in a rolling window).

Discounts and term mechanics
- Yearly term discount schedule (example): 10% off list for year 1 commit, additional incremental discounts for multi-year (eg +3% in year 2, +2% in year 3) tied to committed ARR. We can fix discounts as blended in a multi-year SOW.
- Effective discount depends on prepay ratio and true-up rate; higher upfront prepay gets steeper unit price.

Operational rules we recommend
- Monthly reporting with token-level burn export and per-route attribution.
- Quarterly reconciliation window (14 days) for true-ups and rollover decisions.
- Rollover cap, expiration policy for credits (e.g., credits expire after 12 months unless otherwise negotiated).

I attached RAMP_TABLE.xlsx with a worked example: 3-year, $3.6M total commit; 60% upfront wallet; 20% carry-forward cap; quarterly true-up pricing at list + 10%. The SOW draft includes invoicing cadence.

If this matches your procurement constraints, I can run the numbers with your forecast and return a final SOW for legal to review.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RAMP_TABLE.xlsx (xlsx), SOW_draft.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Committed spend mechanics — internal pricing notes

Marcus — quick notes from finance and ops: 

- Finance prefers invoices that map to quarters (laddered cliffs are easier) but can support sinking-fund billing if we split the wallet over quarterly invoices (i.e., bill the 60% prepay as 4 quarterly invoices to match Acme's fiscal ops).
- Discount floor: legal wants to avoid compounding discount stacking across guardians; propose blended discount calculation in SOW to keep effective unit pricing stable.
- True-up collection: allow 30 days after the reconciliation window for PO issuance or automatic charge depending on Acme preference.

I'll let Karthik weigh in on how conservative we should be with the carry-forward cap.

-Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
VP, Deals & Pricing
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: sinking-fund with quarterly invoices + capped rollover (draft SOW)

Samantha / Jorge —

Following internal alignment, please find the proposed approach for Acme's 36-month commitment:

Highlights (draft)
- Total committed value: $3,600,000 over 36 months (example numbers; we will adjust to your forecast).
- Prepay wallet: 60% of total ($2,160,000) billed across first four quarters (quarterly invoices of $540k) to accommodate Acme's AR process.
- Monthly amortization: the wallet is amortized against committed monthly velocity; bookkeeping reduces wallet balance each month.
- Carry-forward/cap: unused credits at quarter boundary carry into next quarter up to 20% of that next quarter's committed units. Credits above the cap expire unless Acme opts to roll them forward with a replenishment invoice.
- Quarterly true-up: 14-day reconciliation window after quarter close. Overages are charged at list + 10% if wallet is exhausted; we can negotiate an alternate overage rate if Acme prefers a fixed top-up schedule.
- Rollover exceptions: one-time 30% cushion allowed in year 1 for launch seasonality; subsequent years revert to standard carry-forward cap.
- Discounts: effective blended discount equals base model discount (10% year 1, +3% year 2, +2% year 3) adjusted by prepay ratio; I included a worked example in the attached RAMP_TABLE.xlsx.

Next steps
- Please confirm the high-level mechanics above and provide the final forecast numbers.
- If approved, we'll issue an SOW and DocuSign package (link below) for signature.

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/sign?token=XYZ-ACME-2027
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2027-01

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the worked example.

Thanks — Marcus
